test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which was the first social media site?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Six Degrees**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **SixDegrees.com **was a **social networking service website** that ran from **1997 to 2000** and was based on the Web of Contacts premise.
 
• It was named after the six degrees of separation idea and allowed users to list both internal and exterior contacts; external contacts were encouraged to join the site.
 
• People who confirmed a relationship with an existing user but did not register with the site continued to get email updates and solicitations on a regular basis.
 
• **Users could send messages and bulletin board articles** to persons in their first, second, and third degrees, as well as check who they were connected to on the site.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Friendster **was a social networking game established by Jonathan Abrams in Mountain View, California, and launched in March 2003.
 
• **LinkedIn **is a website and mobile app that focuses on business and jobs in the United States.
 
• **Myspace** is a popular social media platform located in the United States. The site was the first social network to reach a global audience, and it had a tremendous impact on technology, pop culture, and music when it was launched on August 1, 2003. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Social media **are interactive digital channels that allow people to share information, ideas, and other kinds of expression through virtual communities and networks.
 
• Users typically use web-based programmes on their computers or download services that provide social media capabilities to their mobile devices to access social media services (e.g., smartphones and tablets). Individuals, communities, and organisations can share, co-create, discuss, participate in, and edit user-generated or self-curated content uploaded online as a result of their interactions with various electronic services.
